subject: Human Evolution
title: Hearth Technology
description: Learn Hearth Technology in one minute.

hook.text: Ice age hearths weren't random fires. Some were stone-lined, banked with earth, and built to last days.

buildup.text: Strategic hearth placement inside shelters maximized heat reflection from cave walls or bone structures.

discovery.text: Some sites show multiple hearths arranged for different functions: cooking, warmth, and tool-making.

twist.text: Fuel choice mattered: bone burns hotter and longer than wood—useful when forests were distant.

climax.text: Hearth engineering was a survival technology as sophisticated as any tool in the ice age toolkit.

punchline.text: A well-built fire was high technology.

quiz.question: Why did ice age people sometimes burn bones instead of wood?
options: Bone burns hotter and longer, and wood was scarce on the steppe
